guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / asthma attack; BTS/SIGN Asthma guidelines
title: Severe asthma attack at a charity fun run
setting: Outdoor charity fun run. 30F participant sitting on a grass verge, struggling to breathe and communicating in short, gasping, single-word sentences.
verdictExplanation: Severe respiratory distress: breathing fast (27/min), low oxygen saturation (88%), unable to speak in full sentences, and using accessory muscles. Sick: immediate treatment and 999 needed.

shared.response: Alert but highly anxious and distressed

er.exposure: Outdoors, mild weather, wearing a superhero costume

history.history: Asthma attack triggered by exertion during the fun run
history.drugs: Salbutamol (blue inhaler) in her bum-bag, has taken several puffs without relief
history.additional: Expresses fear and anxiety about not being able to catch her breath

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority first aid management?

options.text: Sit her upright, help her take her blue salbutamol inhaler (up to 10 puffs via spacer), and call 999
Lay her flat on her back, raise her legs, and tell her to breathe slowly
Administer her brown preventer inhaler immediately
Encourage her to walk to the first aid tent 200m away to rest

followUp.explanation: Sit the patient upright to ease breathing. Use the blue reliever inhaler (salbutamol) - 1 puff every 30-60 seconds up to 10 puffs. Call 999 as she has taken inhalers without relief and cannot speak in sentences. Never lay a breathless patient flat or make them walk.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Sit upright, keep calm. Help her use her reliever (blue) inhaler. Call 999 if no improvement.
levelFlags.erNotes: Severe acute asthma. Monitor pulse oximetry. Give high-flow oxygen, assist with salbutamol via spacer or nebulizer if available. Sit upright, prepare for emergency transport. Do not let her walk.
